caption: The drawing is done in pencil on a beige or light brown piece of paper, and it features three views of a chair: the seat plan (top view), the front view, and the side view. The seat plan is rectangular with the back edge measuring 14 1/2 inches and the front edge 17 3/4 inches, spanning a depth of 16 inches. The front view displays the chair's straight backrest, square seat, and four legs with decorative carved patterns; the backrest features a rectangular panel on top and a section with a scroll-like ornamental design below. Each front leg has carved detail, while the feet slightly curve outward. The side view reveals the S-shaped curve of the back leg, which continues upward into the curved backrest, both ending in spiral designs. Dimensions are marked next to the respective features: the total height of the chair is 34 1/2 inches, the seat height is 17 inches, and the seat's depth is 14 3/4 inches. Text in the upper right identifies the drawing as a chair from about 1820, attributed to the Brooklyn Museum, at a scale of 1/8 inch, and signed by Robert Brigadier with the date 4/27/36. All lines, forms, and details are rendered in monochrome pencil shading.
title: Side Chair
